description: Third-person-singular agreement for the 'go to school' routine (audit commit ad3641395), rule en-third-person-school-routine. A He/She/It subject + 'go to school' is conjugated to 'goes to school'. expectedStatus/expectedCorrection are the VERIFIED output of correctWithTutorRules('en') on current main (captured from the live engine).
fp_risk_note: This rule overlaps heavily with en-step5-subject-verb-agreement, which runs EARLIER and also rewrites 'He go ...' -> 'He goes ...'. So plain 'He go to school' is attributed to step5-SVA, not this rule. This rule's id only surfaces when step5-SVA is suppressed by an SVA temporal blocker that is NOT 'yesterday' (on <weekday>, in <year>, last <season>, <N> hours ago) — those block step5-SVA but the routine rule only bows out on 'yesterday'. Hence the positives carry such markers. Negatives stress: already-conjugated ('He goes to school'); 'yesterday', where this rule correctly stands down AND en-yesterday-irregular instead rewrites go->went ('He go to school yesterday' -> 'He went to school yesterday.', this rule's id absent); and first-person subjects (correct English). A regression that reorders these rules or widens the blocker set will shift which rule fires here.

positive.input: He go to school on Monday
positive.expectedCorrection: He goes to school on Monday.
positive.notes: 'on Monday' blocks step5-SVA (an SVA temporal blocker) but is not 'yesterday', so the routine rule fires: go -> goes.
'in 2024' suppresses step5-SVA; routine rule conjugates go -> goes. She subject.

positive.input: He go to school last summer
positive.expectedCorrection: He goes to school last summer.
positive.notes: 'last summer' (a season, not 'yesterday') suppresses step5-SVA; routine rule fires.

negative.notes: Already correctly conjugated — must not fire.

FP-stress / interplay: this rule correctly stands down on 'yesterday'. The output IS corrected — but by en-yesterday-irregular-beginner-past (go -> went), NOT this rule, so this rule's id must be absent from appliedRuleIds.
First-person subject is correct English; the rule is He/She/It only.
FP guard (question, second person): 'you' is not He/She/It, so no conjugation; stays unchanged.
FP guard (question, no 'to school'): the routine rule needs 'go to school'; bare 'go' in a question stays unchanged.
FP guard: does question must keep go as base-form.
FP guard: plural do question is outside third-person singular correction.

negative.input: Does she go to school every day?
negative.expectedCorrection: Does she go to school every day?
negative.notes: FP guard: question-like input must block the school routine rule even with every day present.

negative.input: When does he go to school?
negative.expectedCorrection: When does he go to school?
negative.notes: FP guard: wh-question with does keeps go in base form.
